name: Laser char
sub: A CO₂ beam rasters a die into card, one scan line at a time. Each line is a gaussian burn: past a threshold the paper scorches tan → brown → black, sinks, and the tooth is burned smooth; heat browns the fibers around it. Vector cuts go through: a charred kerf opening onto the dark bed below.

entry.call: fx.run(o, W, H, dpr, { S, clips })

in.o: params object — keys below; every length in CSS px
in.dpr: device px per CSS px (density is physical: marks per CSS px²)

x.S: params of every effect keyed by id; the stock this prints on is read from S[printsOn]
x.clips: Float32Array alpha per name (die), from FXSET.clips('fx-12-laser', W, H, dpr, o) on a thread with fonts
x.umask: optional: clips.umask — a typed or image mask (mShape type | image)

out.lin: Float32Array W·H·3, linear-light sRGB (encode with FX.toRGBA(R,"image",W,H))
out.ink: Float32Array W·H, absorbance / coverage (FX.toRGBA(R,"ink",…) = film positive)
out.stock: Float32Array W·H, stock height (FX.toRGBA(R,"stock",…) = normalized height map)

light.note: az = direction the light comes FROM (screen degrees; 0 = right, 90 = below); el = elevation above the sheet

deterministic: yes — every random draw is a hash of (position, seed); same inputs → same pixels in the same engine

params.label: Die
params.note: what the die (or type) is: an invented mark (compass, sun, crescent, knot, a monogram from the text), a word, or a ring seal

params.label: Text
params.note: set in Archivo 800 for word, seal and monogram (its first letter)

params.label: Size
params.note: die height as a share of the plate

params.label: Power
params.note: beam power in the raster; dose ∝ power ÷ speed ÷ pitch

params.label: Speed
params.note: head speed (relative); faster = less dose per line

params.label: Line pitch
params.note: distance between scan lines; clamped to ≥ 2 device px

params.label: Scan angle
params.note: direction the head travels

params.label: Spot
params.note: beam radius σ in focus

params.label: Defocus
params.note: 0 = in focus; out of focus the spot widens and its peak drops

params.label: Power ramp
params.note: power falls across the raster, to 15 % at 1

params.label: Turnaround burn
params.note: extra dose where the head slows to reverse at each line end

params.label: Heat halo
params.note: fibers browned around the burn

params.label: Ablation
params.note: how far the surface sinks at full char

params.label: Vector cut
params.note: outline = the die cut out at an offset; tag = a rounded tag with a hole

params.label: Cut offset
params.note: distance from the die edge to the cut

params.label: Tabs
params.note: uncut bridges that hold the part

params.label: Card thickness
params.note: sizes the card edge's shadow on the ground in the kerf

params.label: Ground below · L
params.note: OKLCH lightness (0 black … 1 white)

params.label: Ground below · C

limits.why: most hues leave sRGB above ~.26 and get chroma-reduced

params.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

params.label: Ground below · h
params.note: OKLCH hue angle

params.label: Seed
params.note: every random draw in the effect hangs off this one number

recipe: Scan lines at the pitch (≥ 2 device px), at the scan angle. Dose at a pixel = Σ over nearby lines of power ÷ speed × the beam's gaussian, integrated over the pixel (erf) — anti-aliased lines at any angle.
Firing gate = the die clip sampled at each line's centerline, softened by the spot along the scan; the head's turnaround adds dose just inside the edges it reverses at.
Defocus widens σ and lowers the peak (same energy, larger spot): paler, softer, lines merging. A power ramp can run across the raster.
Char = 1 − e^(−k·(dose − threshold)) → an OKLab ramp tan → brown → black, multiplied into the stock albedo (fibers char darker). Heat halo = the dose spread a few px, browning fibers first.
Relief: ablation sinks the surface with dose; the tooth is burned smooth; a fine char crust. Lit by the sheet light (grooves catch it on one wall).
Vector cut: a kerf along the die outline (offset) or a tag; tabs leave bridges. The kerf opens onto the ground below, shaded by the card edge toward the light; its walls are charred.
